title: A Fresh Start Abroad
subtitle: Maya moves abroad to study.
paras: Maya had always dreamed of studying abroad. When the opportunity finally came — a place at a university in a foreign country — she was definitely nervous, but she was also more excited than she had ever been.

The hardest part, right at the beginning, was finding accommodation. She searched online late into the night, and it was necessary to be careful: some adverts seemed designed to trick or embarrass newcomers. In the end, a colleague on her course was happy to recommend a small flat beside a beautiful park. Maya could hardly believe her luck.

The government paperwork, on the other hand, was a nightmare. She had to register her new address immediately, and the queue at the office stretched out of the door. To her surprise, the official was patient and shared exactly the knowledge she needed. "It is a privilege to help students who take things seriously," he said with a smile.

University life was not quite what she had imagined. She was determined to achieve excellent results, and she knew that would take real discipline. The environment was friendly but fiercely competitive. By February, however, she felt calm and independent, and the move that had once terrified her had turned out, quite unexpectedly, to be the best decision of her life.
discuss: What made Maya's first months difficult, and what helped her through them? What would you tell someone who is about to move to another country?

items.trick: Double P: an OPPortunity is worth two Ps.

items.clue: from or in another country
items.trick: E before I, and a silent G. The word itself breaks the rules.

items.clue: certainly; without any doubt
items.trick: FINITE is hiding inside: de-FINITE-ly. There is no A anywhere.

items.trick: BEGIN doubles its N before -ING.

items.clue: a place to live or stay
items.trick: It is big enough for two Cs and two Ms.

items.clue: needed; essential
items.trick: One Collar, two Sleeves: one C, two Ss.

items.trick: Two Rs and two Ss: you go Really Red and Smile Shyly.

items.trick: Double L, then LEAGUE: colleagues play in the same league.

items.trick: One C, two Ms: re + COMMEND.

items.trick: It starts with BEAU: Big Elephants Are Useful.

items.trick: GOVERN + MENT. Keep the N you hardly hear.

speaking: Talk about a time you — or someone you know — started something new: a course, a job, or a move to a new city. Use at least six of the words. For two of them, spell the word out loud, part by part: "ac – com – mo – da – tion".
